item.title: Foundry-Fabricated Silicon Nitride Grating Arrays with Uniform Power Distribution at Visible Wavelengths
item.description: arXiv:2610.30387v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multiplexed optical biosensors are widely deployed to read out many biological targets in parallel. However, their channel count and integration density are limited by the photonic network that delivers light to individual sensing sites. Existing on-chip networks have been largely developed for phased arrays and image projection, where performance is assessed through an aggregate radiation pattern rather than the local intensity at each output. In this Letter, we demonstrate a novel bus-and-tap network architecture for massively parallel multiplexed optical delivery. The network uses cascaded directional couplers with individually designed interaction lengths, allowing for arbitrary, user-defined illumination patterns not possible with conventional binary tree architectures. We experimentally validated our proposed architecture with 46 visible-wavelength grating emitter channels designed for uniform illumination at 40 $\mu$m pitch in a commercial 300-mm silicon nitride foundry process, achieving an emitted-intensity coefficient of variation of 9.3% at 530 nm, and 8.8% under band-integrated illumination from 550 nm to 650 nm. These results provide a route to scalable visible-light delivery for sensing, imaging, neural interfaces, and parallel optical addressing in quantum systems.
item.dc:creator: Amged Alquliah, Xiaoxin Wang, Jifeng Liu, Anthony Rizzo

item.title: Black-Hole Ringdown from Photon-Sphere Modes in an Elastic Analogue
item.description: arXiv:2610.30396v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quasinormal modes (QNMs) govern the ringdown of black holes, yet their physical origin and experimental accessibility remain limited. Here we create an elastic analogue of a black hole using a curved metallic shell engineered to emulate a Schwarzschild-like metric, and directly probe its vibrational dynamics in the time domain. Following impulsive excitation, the elastic system exhibits a clear ringdown response, providing a tangible analogue of black-hole ringing. The underlying modes are flexural vibrations localized near the photon sphere. A reduction of the thin-shell elastic equations yields a photon-sphere effective potential and predicts the dependence of the localized-mode frequencies on azimuthal order. Crucially, they persist even when boundary reflections are strongly suppressed, demonstrating that their confinement is governed by a curvature-induced effective potential rather than by cavity boundaries. This platform enables direct access to quasinormal modes through both their temporal decay and spectral signatures, establishing a direct connection between photon-sphere dynamics and ringdown. More broadly, our results identify curvature-induced trapping as a general mechanism for wave localization and dissipation in open systems.
item.dc:creator: Jiaoqing Wang, Chenni Xu, Sophia Purow, S\'ebastien Guenneau, Patrick Sebbah

item.title: Laser with $7\times10^{-18}$ stability
item.description: arXiv:2610.30532v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report a laser with record frequency stability, based on a 21 cm cryogenic silicon cavity. For best short-term stability, the cavity operates at 6 K to minimize Brownian thermal noise and achieves a fractional stability of $7\times10^{-18}$ between 2 to 50 s of averaging time and 2.5 mHz linewidth. For best long-term stability the cavity operates at 16 K, where silicon has a zero-crossing of thermal expansion. Slightly increased thermal noise limits the performance to $9\times10^{-18}$, consistent with the expected temperature scaling, but the long-term performance is improved. The laser then has a linewidth of 2.9 mHz and long-term frequency drift less than 4 {\mu}Hz s$^{-1}$. The laser is used to enhance the performance of a state-of-the-art Sr lattice clock, operating with Rabi and Ramsey interrogation times beyond 10 s.
item.dc:creator: Ben Lewis, Zoey Z. Hu, Dahyeon Lee, Kyungtae Kim, William Warfield, Kai Zhou, Daniele Nicolodi, Thomas Legero, Uwe Sterr, Fritz Riehle, Jun Ye

item.title: Efficient third-harmonic generation in high-Q tantalum pentoxide microcavities
item.description: arXiv:2610.30579v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nonlinear harmonic generation in microcavities offers a compelling route toward energy efficient on-chip short-wavelength coherent light sources, enabled by tight optical confinement within compact mode volumes and flexible dispersion engineering. Tantalum pentoxide (Ta2O5) photonic platforms are particularly promising for realizing such nonlinear processes: their broad transparency window (280-8000 nm) supports broadband operation, their large bandgap suppresses two-photon absorption, and their thick-film deposition capability enables dispersion management--features that can collectively enhance the performance of nonlinear light sources. Here, we demonstrate, to the best of our knowledge, the first efficient third-harmonic generation (THG) in high-Q Ta2O5 microcavities. These microcavities feature smooth surfaces and high loaded Q factors up to 2.67X10^6, thereby facilitating nonlinear interactions. Through dispersion engineering, efficient THG is realized in both suspended microdisks and monolithic microrings under telecom-band continuous-wave laser pumping, as confirmed by optical spectra, visible-light microscopy, and the near-cubic pump-power dependence of the conversion efficiency. This work lays a foundation for chip-scale f-3f self-referencing of frequency combs and next-generation integrated nonlinear photonics.
item.dc:creator: Xinke Xing, Yixuan Yang, Xinzhi Zheng, Renhong Gao, Li Deng, Jintian Lin, Ya Cheng

item.title: Alignment-Free Optical Combining with Scalar-Message Expectation Propagation Detection for Distributed Multi-Aperture Coherent Reception
item.description: arXiv:2610.30600v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose an alignment-free distributed multi-aperture optical receiver with a single coherent front end, in which the differential delays between apertures are large. The branch signals are optically combined without inter-branch delay or phase alignment. Large differential delays produce separated tap clusters, forming a sparse ISI channel with long memory. Scalar-message expectation propagation exploits this sparsity to recover the transmitted symbols. Simulations show lower BER than equal-area single-aperture reception and no clear BER degradation over the tested delay spans. As the maximum differential delay increases from 100.5 to 200.5 symbol periods, the channel span nearly doubles, while the factor-graph edge count increases by only about 1.5\%. The trade-off is higher BER than ideal coherent combining schemes in exchange for fewer coherent front ends than digital combining and no inter-branch delay or phase alignment before optical combining.
item.dc:creator: Mingwen Zhu, Yiqun Zhang, Liyu Sun, Ming Liu, Changwei Wang, Jiayin Xue

item.title: Metasurface engineering of transient photothermal responses for vibrational imaging at living interfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.30610v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chemical transformations at biological interfaces are central to cellular function, yet the weak vibrational signals associated with subtle molecular changes limit their spatially resolved observation. Here, we present metasurface-driven mid-infrared photothermal imaging (MetaMIP), which uses resonantly engineered metasurfaces to amplify molecular temperature modulation while retaining rapid thermal recovery. Visible-light detection converts this response into submicrometre maps of individual nanoparticles and biological cells. In living cells, MetaMIP resolves spatially distinct chemical changes during enzymatic lipid conversion across the cell membrane. These results demonstrate the potential of engineered photothermal interfaces for mapping chemical composition and tracking its evolution during reactions.
item.dc:creator: Zhibin Hu, Tianrun Zhang, Jiayu Ding, Pengcheng Fu, Ziyang Huang, Bo Chen, Bangjie Song, Minglu Li, Xinyu Deng, Quan D. Zhou, Delong Zhang, Siying Peng

item.title: Reconfigurable Free-Space Optical Interconnects
item.description: arXiv:2610.30757v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Free-space optical interconnects can support many low-data-rate channels while avoiding the cost, energy consumption, and packaging constraints of optical waveguide- or fiber-based systems that are widely used today. We propose a free-space optical interconnect system based on reconfigurable micromirror arrays, and show that it scales favorably due to its two-dimensional scaling. We discuss the channel count scaling model, compare our demonstration with theory, and project a channel count above 10,000 to achieve 100 Tbps with slow channels (e.g., <10 Gbps). In a proof-of-concept system with a piston-motion micromirror array, we demonstrate nine channels that are simultaneously optimized. The optimization enables -21.7 dB of average worst-case crosstalk for a channel pitch equal to twice the beam radius, a smaller channel spacing than that required in flat tip-tilt mirrors. The optimization flow is further investigated for different channel spacings, simultaneous illumination, and different numbers of outputs, which generally achieve smaller worst-case crosstalk than the flat tip-tilt mirror case. Overall, the work demonstrates the advantage of piston-motion micromirrors in the proposed optical interconnects.
item.dc:creator: Jaekwon Lee, Carson G. Valdez, Anne R. Kroo, David A. B. Miller, Olav Solgaard

item.title: Light pulse propagation through a dielectric slab. II. Two roads to the same field: numerical cross-validation of local (FDTD-ADE) and non-local (retarded integral-equation) solutions
item.description: arXiv:2610.30833v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Paper I of this series (arXiv:2610.29336) solves, via the retarded Green's functions, the local differential equations governing light propagation in a plane-parallel dielectric slab, obtaining a pair of retarded integral equations that represent, at the continuum level, the microscopic multiple-scattering picture underlying the local formulation. The two formulations are thus proven to be analytically equivalent. The local system of differential equations is then solved numerically with a finite-difference time-domain scheme (FDTD-ADE). This report closes the loop by solving the retarded integral equations directly, without passing through the local formulation, and comparing the result with the FDTD-ADE solution under the same physical and material conditions. The two independently implemented, structurally different numerical schemes agree within 0.02-1.3% for the reported reflected and transmitted energy fractions; the absorbed fraction, computed independently in both schemes from the Lorentz damping term rather than merely inferred from 1-R-T, agrees closely between the two methods, to the precision reported. Both solutions are also compared with an exact reference, the Airy formula weighted over the pulse spectrum: the direct solution reproduces it to within 0.3%, and its Richardson extrapolation to all digits shown. The agreement persists for a few-cycle pulse and for a sub-wavelength slab, where naive fixed-point iteration of the integral equations is not a practical convergent strategy. A complementary set of movie-style, nine-frame visualizations is also presented, illustrating the same equivalence directly in the field rather than only in integrated observables. To the author's knowledge, a direct numerical cross-validation of these two formulations in this genuinely time-dependent regime has not previously been reported.
item.dc:creator: Giancarlo Reali

item.title: All-photonic millimeter-wave and terahertz signal core at room and cryogenic temperatures
item.description: arXiv:2610.30857v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Millimeter-wave and terahertz technologies offer new opportunities for high-capacity communications, sensing, and quantum systems, but electronic signal chains above 100 GHz are limited by weak sources, noisy receivers, and lossy interconnects. Photonic approaches mitigate these constraints by enabling chip-scale high-frequency components, yet existing implementations generally retain lossy off-chip electrical or free-space links, hindering dense and compact integration for cryogenic or space-constrained settings. Here, we show a monolithic lithium tantalate photonic chip, termed a signal core, which generates, modulates, routes, and detects continuous-wave signals at discrete frequencies between 100 GHz and 2.5 THz. The architecture integrates high-frequency functional modules on chip and uses exclusively fiber-based optical interfaces. Bidirectional coherent electro-optic conversion enables signal generation, detection, and nanosecond-scale amplitude and phase modulation, while micro-coplanar striplines interconnect the modules into an end-to-end signal chain on a single chip. Our modules achieve single-photon electro-optic coupling rates of g_0/2\pi=10 kHz and peak drive-power-normalized photon-flux conversion efficiencies of 1.0%/mW for generation and 0.5%/mW for detection. It also operates at 4 K in a dilution refrigerator through the same fiber-only optical links. Together, these capabilities establish an all-photonic platform for millimeter-wave-to-terahertz systems and offer a broadly applicable architecture for applications constrained by electrical-interconnect loss, heat load, and footprint.
item.dc:creator: Jiawen Liu, Chengli Wang, Aleksei Gaier, Tianyi Zhang, Gabriel J\"ulg, Yazan Lampert, Andr\'e Garcia Primo, Alessandro Tomasino, Hua Li, Xin Ou, Ileana-Cristina Benea-Chelmus

item.title: Laser-design methodology for extending an available wavelength range of dual-wavelength injection-seeded laser
item.description: arXiv:2610.30897v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper describes a method for expanding the applicable wavelength range of dual-wavelength oscillation injection-locked lasers. Special focus is placed on the laser design that enables simultaneous oscillations at both the gain center and gain tail, requiring the most stringent requirements. We show that a sufficient performance can be achieved by introducing a wavelength-dependence property onto the output coupling mirror, without giving any losses in the laser resonator. We also show how we can determine such wavelength-dependent property on the basis of experimental measurements. Using the designed output-coupler, in practices, we demonstrate simultaneous oscillations with an equal output power, across a variety of wavelength combinations of near the gain center and around the gain tail in which the wavelength separation amounts 60 nm at the most.
item.dc:creator: Ayaka Hashimoto, Tetsuto Watanabe. Sota Kobayashi, Megumi Otose, Ken'ichi Nakagawa, Masayuki Katsuragawa

item.title: Intrinsic Angular Momentum Contribution to the Sagnac Response of a Rotating Helical Optical Fiber
item.description: arXiv:2610.30898v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate rotation-induced phase accumulation of structured light in a mechanically rotating uniform helical optical fiber using a four-component optical Dirac-like equation. In the paraxial and weak-geometry regime, the intrinsic dynamics contain a torsion-induced geometric coupling and a mechanical rotation--angular-momentum coupling. We show that, in a common-path mirror-reflection geometry, both the torsion-induced geometric phase and the conventional area-dependent Sagnac contribution cancel over a complete round trip, whereas the intrinsic rotation--angular-momentum phase survives. The surviving phase depends on the intrinsic total angular momentum of the structured optical mode and provides a common-path interferometric route for probing intrinsic angular momentum effects in rotational sensing.
item.dc:creator: Lili Yang, Pengming Zhang, Longlong Feng

item.title: Efficient Modeling of 3D-Printed Freeform Waveguides with a Transformation Optics-Based Beam Propagation Method
item.description: arXiv:2610.31004v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An efficient numerical method is introduced for simulating wave propagation in 3D-printed freeform waveguides, referred to as photonic wire bonds (PWBs). This approach integrates transformation optics (TO) with curvilinear meshing to map the original 3D freeform PWB structure onto a straight waveguide, which possesses anisotropic material characteristics. The resulting waveguide is then analyzed using an anisotropic full-vectorial beam propagation method (BPM). To validate the performance and effectiveness of the proposed TO-BPM algorithm, a comparison is made with the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) technique. Our approach reduces the simulation time by more than two orders of magnitude, depending on the degree of trajectory bending, in combination with a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 3.9% in power transmission simulation relative to the FDTD.
item.dc:creator: Sina Foroutan-Barenji, Jonas Krimmer, Stefan Singer, Christian Koos, Wolfgang Freude

item.title: Effective-action formulation of $\mathbf{k}$-odd bianisotropy and unidirectional polarization rotation in nonlocal temporal metamaterials
item.description: arXiv:2610.31022v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive the effective action of temporal metamaterials up to first order in spatial derivatives through a multiscale analysis of the electromagnetic Lagrangian density. We show that the first-order spatial correction gives rise to an effective bianisotropic coupling tensor that is odd in the wavevector $\mathbf{k}$. Remarkably, chiral, pseudochiral, and omega-type bianisotropic responses emerge as distinct directional manifestations of a single nonlocal coupling tensor, even when the underlying electric and magnetic response tensors remain symmetric. Furthermore, we establish a framework for analyzing Lorentz reciprocity based on the Hessian of the effective action. We demonstrate that Lorentz reciprocity is preserved in the presence of omega-type coupling but is broken when chiral or pseudochiral coupling emerges. This nonreciprocity manifests as the unidirectional rotations of normalized Stokes vectors incurred by Floquet-engineered chirality and pseudochirality.
item.dc:creator: Neng Wang, Guo Ping Wang

item.title: The Mechanism of Chirality in Plasmonic Structures: Asymmetric Resonance Modes
item.description: arXiv:2610.31045v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This study presents a theoretical framework for understanding the mechanism of chirality generation and circular dichroism (CD) in chiral nanostructures, with a particular focus on the role of asymmetric plasmon resonance mode distributions. Although previous studies have linked chiroptical properties to resonance differences, the specific nature and origin of these differences have not been fully elucidated. Here, we provide a more detailed explanation by quantitatively analyzing the asymmetric electric-field components arising from mode asymmetry. Specifically, we examine the near-field symmetry of individual nanorods and corner-stacked coupled structures (CSCS). The results demonstrate that chirality arises from asymmetric electric-field distributions, which give rise to distinct phase and amplitude responses of the electromagnetic fields in the composite structure under right-handed circularly polarized (RCP) and left-handed circularly polarized (LCP) illumination. The absorption and CD spectra, which exhibit distinct features around $910\,\mathrm{nm}$, support this mechanism and provide valuable insights into the design of chiroptical materials. The proposed mechanism is not restricted to a specific chiral structure or resonance and offers a broader explanation for the generation of circular dichroism.
item.dc:creator: Abduweli Abdukerim

item.title: Shaping Near Fields of Photonic Modes into Topological Textures
item.description: arXiv:2610.31207v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Topological textures of light, such as optical vortices and skyrmions, are attractive for high-density information encoding and light-matter interactions. In the near field, topologies have primarily been realized using polaritonic platforms that inherently tie the platform to the material dispersion, limiting their footprint due to propagation losses and restricting their operating spectral region. Here, we introduce a route to shape near-field topologies through the geometric engineering of a dielectric metasurface supporting a quasi-bound state in the continuum resonance, without the need for polaritonic surface waves. In-plane deformation of our metasurface bars conserves their resonance-driven near-fields locally, so that the metasurface geometry and the polarization of the illuminating light dictate the generated topology. By shaping silicon unit cells into geometries with rotational symmetry, we create optical topologies with controllable topological charge. Using phase-resolved scattering-type near-field optical microscopy, we experimentally characterize high-purity resonance-locked topologies such as vortices in concentric rings and topological charge doublets in Archimedean spirals. In contrast to conventional topological textures, our purely photonic mode-based field textures are stationary standing waves in the radial direction, without relying on surface-wave propagation or polaritonic dispersion, establishing a spectrally and spatially scalable platform for near-field topological photonics.
item.dc:creator: Jonas Biechteler, Michael Hirler, Connor Heimig, Martin Barkey, Haoran Ren, Stefan A. Maier, Enrico Ba\`u, Andreas Tittl

item.title: Second- and third-order nonlinearities in silicon nitride waveguides via heterogeneous integration of lithium niobate membranes
item.description: arXiv:2610.31243v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Thick, dispersion-engineered silicon nitride is a leading platform for integrated third-order nonlinear optics, supporting supercontinuum and frequency comb generation. However, it lacks the second-order nonlinearity required by many applications. Here we bond pre-fabricated x-cut thin-film lithium niobate membranes onto finished silicon nitride waveguides as a back-end step, compatible with commercially fabricated waveguides. A single silicon nitride waveguide generates an octave-spanning supercontinuum and, through the lithium niobate membrane, concurrent second-harmonic, sum- and difference-frequency generation. These results open new possibilities for thick silicon nitride photonics, from visible light generation to on-chip $f$-$2f$ comb self-referencing, a key step towards miniaturised timing and navigation quantum technologies.
item.dc:creator: Natale G. Pruiti, Cosmin Suciu, Eugenio Di Gaetano, Jonathan M. Silver, Douglas J. Paul, Marc Sorel

item.title: A New Twist on Astigmatic Transformation: Beyond Laguerre-Gaussian Beams
item.description: arXiv:2610.31313v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Astigmatic transformation is widely used to convert the azimuthal phase structure of Laguerre-Gaussian vortex beams into intensity patterns from which the topological charge can be read out. Here, we show that this phase-to-intensity conversion is not just restricted to the Laguerre-Gaussian radial profile. We derive analytical expressions for the astigmatically transformed high-order Bessel--Gauss and perfect optical vortex fields, and find that, despite their substantially different radial structures, the number of intensity minima is directly set by the accumulated azimuthal phase winding. Numerical simulations and experimental measurements on both beam families confirm this result, establishing astigmatic transformation as a direct probe of the topological charge of scalar structured optical fields. We further extend the approach to non-separable vector Bessel-Gauss beams, in which the spatial and polarization degrees of freedom are coupled, and show that polarization-resolved detection allows the topological charge of the constituent spatial modes to be determined independently.
item.dc:creator: Gabriela Flores-Cova, Bikash Kumar Das, Carmelo Rosales-Guzman, Valeria-Rodriguez-Fajardo, Camilo Granados

item.title: Predictive electronic feedback control for narrow-linewidth lasers
item.description: arXiv:2610.31396v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Narrow-linewidth lasers are essential for various key atom-laser interaction processes and optical setups in quantum coherent control, quantum precision measurement, and quantum information science. The Pound-Drever-Hall (PDH) technique is the standard method for the frequency-stabilization of narrow-linewidth lasers, but the inherent time delay in its feedback loop inevitably induces excessive phase noise, commonly known as servo bumps. Previous solutions primarily rely on additional optical components outside the electronic feedback control loop. Here, we propose and implement a generic method based on the Smith predictor to address the time-delay issue entirely within the electronic part of the PDH feedback control loop. We systematically demonstrate its capability to suppress phase noise and reduce servo bumps by adding only a single Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) controller to the loop. This class of methods is demonstrated to be conceptually concise with minimal hardware overhead, effective in practice, and holds potential for a wide variety of future applications.
item.dc:creator: Jiatian Liu, Xuan Qi, Xiayang Fan, Shenchao Jin, Yuan Sun

item.title: Nanopillar metasurfaces uniting high optical reflectivity with ultracoherent nanomechanics
item.description: arXiv:2610.31452v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mechanically compliant mirrors are key components in cavity optomechanics. However, the requirements to achieve the best optical and mechanical performance are usually in direct competition. A high reflectivity for tightly focused beams entails thick reflectors, whereas ultracoherent flexural nanomechanics necessitates thin membranes. We eliminate this trade-off by introducing high-refractive-index nanopillar metasurfaces on top of a thin membrane. We pattern a 50 micrometer-diameter array of nanopillars to form a photonic crystal. The flat band behavior of guided resonances in the photonic crystal enables a reflectivity of 99.82(1)% for a tightly focused beam of 7 micrometer waist. The combination of two guided resonances creates a 100 nanometer-wide high-reflectivity band around 1550 nanometer. Simultaneously, the nanopillar patterning realizes a density-modulated phononic crystal that isolates an ultracoherent localized mechanical mode with a $Q\cdot f$-product of $2\cdot 10^{14}$Hz. The demonstrated nanopillar metasurfaces enable lightweight mirrors for room-temperature quantum optomechanics and for use as levitated mirrors or lightsails.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Jung, Anastasiia Ciers, Hannes Pfeifer, Albert Hansson, Johanna \"Org{\aa}rd, Daniel Stachanow, Viktor A. Lilja, Philippe Tassin, Witlef Wieczorek

item.title: Observation of Polarization Topology in Magneto-Optical BICs
item.description: arXiv:2610.31498v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Polarization topology in momentum space is a fundamental characteristic of photonic bound states in the continuum (BICs), where the winding of far-field polarization defines a quantized topological charge. Although magneto-optical (MO) BICs combine polarization topology with magnetically tunable chirality, experimental characterization remains challenging because time-reversal symmetry (TRS) breaking complicates eigenpolarization extraction. Here, we experimentally resolve the momentum-space polarization topology of an MO BIC by reconstructing its two-dimensional far-field eigenpolarization texture. We extract the resonant output polarization using singular value decomposition of the polarization-resolved angle-resolved reflection matrix without invoking reciprocity. The reconstructed polarization azimuth winds counterclockwise by 2$\pi$ around the $\Gamma$-point singularity, yielding a topological charge of q = +1. Moreover, the polarization handedness can be reversed solely by varying the magnetic-bias strength, while the field direction and the measured topological charge remain unchanged. A non-Hermitian coupled-mode model traces this reversal to hybridization between the BIC mode and a leaky mode. This work establishes experimental access to momentum-space polarization topology in nonreciprocal photonics, opening a route to explore topological singularities and their evolution under active TRS breaking.
item.dc:creator: Yaqi Li, Mingyu Tong, Fujia Chen, Li Zhang, Rui Zhao, Yuze Hu, Bei Wu, Haiyao Luo, Hongsheng Chen, Yihao Yang

item.title: Confinement of hybridized light modes in nonlinear-optical superpotentials
item.description: arXiv:2610.31643v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we present a spatial and temporal light trapping mechanism induced by coherent frequency conversion. We consider a wave-mixing process, where a pumped nonlinearity mediates a frequency-domain beamsplitter interaction between two signal modes. When these wave modes are counterpropagating, temporally trapped eigenmodes emerge at the zero of the nonlinearity profile. We establish that such spatio-temporal trapping has a direct connection to supersymmetric quantum mechanics, which ensures the existence and robustness of the trapped modes and allows us to derive analytic solutions of the bound eigenmodes. Backwards sum-frequency conversion may thus enable a unique class of active photonic memory devices, whose design parameters are compatible with the state of the art in integrated nonlinear photonics. We propose proof-of-principle experiments to study this nonlinear-optical trapping effect on thin-film lithium niobate. In addition, as a case study, we show how the temporal trap can be used alongside parametric gain. Our work unveils potential applications ranging from classical integrated photonics to multimode quantum nonlinear photonics.
item.dc:creator: Federico Presutti, Ryotatsu Yanagimoto

item.title: Thouless Pumping of One-Dimensional Dark Solitons and Domain Walls
item.description: arXiv:2610.30550v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We predict that quantized transport of dark solitons and domain walls can be observed in mutually sliding optical lattices in both focusing and defocusing nonlinear materials. Two different classes of underlying periodic backgrounds are considered here -- unstaggered and staggered -- which are accurately represented, respectively, by the in-phase and out-of-phase trains of Wannier functions. The nonlinear excitations formed on top of these backgrounds -- dark solitons and domain walls -- are sustained by defocusing or focusing Kerr nonlinearities of the optical medium. Despite non-zero asymptotics, dark solitons and domain walls can still undergo quantized topological transport in dynamically changing refractive index landscape when they and background on which they are constructed are dynamically stable. The extended intervals of propagation constants (and, correspondingly, of the background amplitude) and lattice depths, where stable quantized transport occurs, are identified for both dark solitons and domain walls. Outside these intervals, the quantized transport regime is found to be unstable. Our results extend the concept of nonlinear topological transport from bright to dark soliton states.
item.dc:creator: Fangwei Ye, Aidar H. Ryazhapov, Yaroslav V. Kartashov, Vladimir V. Konotop

item.title: Wavenumber-Aware Deep Learning for Robust Analysis of Raman Spectra
item.description: arXiv:2610.30746v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Machine-learning models for spectroscopy usually treat a spectrum as a fixed-grid intensity vector, leaving the physical coordinate implicit in the array index. Such models are tied to a single sampling grid, spectral range and resolution, which limits their use when measurement conditions change. Here we represent each spectral point as a pair of intensity and wavenumber and compute Transformer positional encodings from the wavenumber itself. On Raman spectra of three bacterial species and their synthetic mixtures, this representation remained robust to noise, sparser sampling and partial spectral coverage across convolutional, residual and Transformer networks. In controlled comparisons, wavenumber-based encoding outperformed index-based and learned encodings under partial observation and retained its performance on sampling grids never seen during training, where index-based encoding degraded. These findings were reproduced on a public 30-isolate bacterial benchmark. Explicit physical coordinates offer a simple route to robust spectral analysis under variable measurement conditions.
item.dc:creator: Jihwan Kim, Jaeseong Heo, Yujin Kim, Sang Bin Yoon, Chanjoong Kim, Kwang-Im Oh, Hyon Bin Na, Kyungwon Kwak, Myeongkee Park, Joonyoung F. Joung

item.title: ADAPT for Science: A Multi-Agent System for Self-Evolving Scientific Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2610.30851v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Scientific discovery often requires identifying a small number of high-performing designs in vast, constrained search spaces. This is difficult when evaluations are costly, feasible solutions are sparse, parameters are strongly coupled, and physical constraints are strict. Recent AI for AI methods can automatically improve algorithms and optimization procedures. However, general purpose approaches are not designed around scientific priors, physical constraints, and limited evaluation budgets. We introduce ADAPT for Science, a multi-agent framework that treats scientific optimization as two coupled decisions: where to search and how to search. ADAPT uses historical designs to identify promising and diverse initial conditions, progressively concentrates computation on favorable search directions, and evolves the optimization procedure from execution feedback. We evaluate ADAPT on the design of gravitational wave detectors using a differentiable physics simulator and eight unseen detector topologies. Under matched scientific evaluation budgets, ADAPT achieves a mean loss of 0.204 +/- 0.101, reducing loss by 54.9% relative to the best classical optimizer and by 62.2% relative to the best general purpose agentic evolution baseline. ADAPT achieves the lowest loss on all unseen topologies among the evaluated baselines. ADAPT provides a step toward scientific optimization systems that continuously learn from prior experience and their own search outcomes.
item.dc:creator: Zhaoran Feng, Yuchen Ni, Jianan Liu, Lemao Liu, Dejing Dou, Kairui Feng

item.title: Entanglement certification of attosecond light fields with photoelectron interferometry
item.description: arXiv:2610.31187v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The emergence of entangled quantum optical states in high-harmonic generation raises a fundamental problem about its characterization, namely, \textit{how can entanglement of extreme-ultraviolet radiation be certified for attosecond light fields?} Here, we provide experimentally accessible separability tests, particularly showing that attosecond photoelectron interferometry provides a direct solution to this problem. This is achieved by a quantum optical treatment of mapping photoelectron interferometry to the measurement of optical correlation functions. This yields a negative-partial-transpose witness for infrared-XUV entanglement and a sufficient witness of genuine multipartite entanglement without auxiliary optical measurements. We evaluate both witnesses on explicit optical states and identify how the protocol can be extended to XUV-XUV entanglement certification. Hence, we establish attosecond photoelectron interferometry as a general framework for entanglement certification across a wide range of optical frequencies.
item.dc:creator: Philipp Stammer

item.title: Rank-One Loss Maximizes the Spectral Response Strength of Passive Full-Order Exceptional Points
item.description: arXiv:2610.31268v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider finite-dimensional non-Hermitian systems in which all modes coalesce at a single exceptional point. For a rank-one anti-Hermitian contribution, the spectral response strength is computed exactly. For passive systems, we then derive a sharp upper bound at fixed exceptional-point decay rate and show that it is reached only when the decay operator has rank one, corresponding to a single independent dissipative direction. This establishes rank-one loss as the optimal configuration for enhancing the response of a full-order exceptional point. The bound holds for arbitrary order and improves on earlier passive estimates beyond second order. Two third-order trimers illustrate the result: a rank-one-loss system saturates the bound, whereas a passive rank-two-loss realization remains below it. The result turns dissipation into a design resource: concentrating the loss into a single effective dissipative direction maximizes the highest-order spectral response of a passive full-order exceptional-point device.
item.dc:creator: Jan Wiersig

item.title: GEM-PIC-RZ: a Galilean electromagnetic particle-in-cell code in quasi-cylindrical geometry with nonuniform grids
item.description: arXiv:2610.31622v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Laser-plasma accelerators span scales from the micrometre wavelength of the driving laser to acceleration lengths of millimetres or metres. Full particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations resolve the laser carrier but are constrained by the Courant condition, whereas quasi-static models are computationally efficient but do not resolve it. We present GEM-PIC-RZ, a quasi-cylindrical implementation of the Galilean electromagnetic PIC scheme. The method retains the slow evolution of the forward field and therefore resolves the laser carrier while allowing a propagation step governed by the evolution of the laser and plasma rather than by the cell size. User-defined nonuniform grids and a charge-conserving regularization of the bubble closure support efficient simulations across these scales. Comparisons with the full PIC code FBPIC show agreement for the laser wake, the depletion and redshift of a few-cycle pulse, and ionization injection; the measured CPU time is about 2\,\% of that for FBPIC in the reported runs; the injected charge carries a model uncertainty of about 15\,\% from the regularization. An envelope model, in contrast, underestimates the depletion of the few-cycle pulse fivefold. Self-injection in a sharp density down-ramp is not yet reproduced and remains an open problem.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Pukhov

item.title: A Photonic Tautochrone: Spatiotemporal Beam Focusing for Enhanced Nonlinear Response
item.description: arXiv:2603.03691v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose to implement an optical analogue of the tautochrone property of the cycloid to allow the focusing of ultrashort pulses inside photonic systems. This allows to enhance nonlinear effects, resulting in orders of magnitude increase of nonlinearity-induced phase shifts, while employing low irradiances. Building upon the optical-mechanical analogy, we show how to produce optical limiters for temporal light pulses, and how to implement temporal bistability and even multistability with large numbers of states. Finally, we move this concept to the quantum realm and predict a tautochrone quantum blockade regime with a stronger antibunching.
item.dc:creator: W. Verstraelen, S. Zanotti, N. W. E. Seet, J. Zhao, D. Sanvitto, J. Zu\~niga-Perez, K. Dini, Y. G. Rubo, T. C. H. Liew

item.title: Second-harmonic generation from an optically levitated KTP nanocrystal in vacuum
item.description: arXiv:2607.02871v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The optically levitated system in vacuum has emerged as a powerful platform for studies of fundamental physics and precision measurements. Although various nanoparticles have been successfully levitated in vacuum, they typically lack the capability to support optical nonlinear processes. Here, we experimentally demonstrate the stable levitation of a potassium titanyl phosphate (KTP) nonlinear nanocrystal in vacuum and investigate its second-harmonic generation (SHG) properties. This levitated system intrinsically provides a pristine dark-background environment with a high signal-to-noise ratio. The trapping laser simultaneously serves as a fundamental light for efficient SHG. Moreover, the polarization of the collected SHG signal is correlated with that of the fundamental laser, providing clear evidence of the optical torque enabling controllable alignment of the nanocrystal with the driving field. Our work establishes a new route, to our knowledge, toward exploring nonlinear optical processes in vacuum levitation systems and designing novel nanodevices with high manipulation agility in a fully contact-free environment.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Yuanbin Jin, Chenli Gao, Jiayu Feng, Yuxuan Hao, Xudong Yu, and Jing Zhang, "Second-harmonic generation from an optically levitated KTP nanocrystal in vacuum," Optica 13, 2179-2185 (2026)
item.dc:creator: Yuanbin Jin, Chenli Gao, Jiayu Feng, Yuxuan Hao, Xudong Yu, Jing Zhang

item.title: Two-Laser Heterodyne Detection System for ALPS II
item.description: arXiv:2610.03376v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Any Light Particle Search II employs a highly sensitive heterodyne detection system to measure an ultra-weak electromagnetic field that is reconverted from axions inside a regeneration cavity (RC). The initial design of the heterodyne system utilized a local oscillator laser (LO) that was resonant with the RC to form an interference beatnote with the weak signal field exiting the cavity. A weakness of this design is that it is possible for the out-of-mode field component of the LO to be larger than the in-mode component, allowing its noise to dominate the optical component of the noise budget and reducing the SNR of the experiment. This problem can be addressed by introducing a second, non-resonant laser as the LO. Since the in-mode light of this laser does not couple to the cavity, significantly more of its power is reflected than when the LO is resonant. We present a model for the measurement noise that predicts these design changes increase the SNR by a factor of roughly 35. This model was then confirmed experimentally by injecting a weak signal to the RC and examining the difference in the sensitivity of the detection system in each of these configurations.
item.dc:creator: Henry Fr\"adrich, Aaron D. Spector, Axel Lindner, Guido M\"uller

item.title: Enhanced Whispering Gallery Mode Phase Shift using Indistinguishable Photon Pairs
item.description: arXiv:2404.17409v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a theoretical investigation of a whispering gallery mode (WGM) resonator coupled to a Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI) and show a bimodal coincidence transmission spectrum when the input state is an indistinguishable photon pair. This is due to the doubled WGM phase shift experienced by the path-entangled state in the interferometer. Further, we model the noise in a WGM resonance shift measurement comparing photon pairs with a coherent state. At least a four-fold improvement in the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) is possible, with clear implications for quantum-enhanced WGM sensing.
item.dc:creator: Callum Jones, Antonio Vidiella-Barranco, Jolly Xavier, Frank Vollmer

item.title: Exact and Asymptotically Complete Robust Verifications of Neural Networks via Ising Solvers
item.description: arXiv:2603.00408v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present an Ising-compatible framework for formal neural-network robustness verification under bounded input perturbations. For piecewise activations (both continuous piecewise-linear and discrete piecewise-constant), the Exact Logarithmic Piecewise Model (Log-PW) provides an exact, sound, and complete formulation with a state-optimal logarithmic encoding, reducing the binary variables per neuron from linear $O(\kappa)$ to information-theoretically minimal logarithmic complexity $O(\lceil \log_2 \kappa \rceil)$ via logarithmic SOS2 (Log-PWL) and SOS1 (Log-PWC) constraints. For general element-wise activations, the Asymptotic Step-Envelope Model (Step-Env) leverages Log-PWC to construct sound, refinable endpoint enclosures. An exact monotonic reduction based on Jordan decomposition further extends this framework to arbitrary non-monotonic activations. We further develop a hybrid Benders solver with output-sensitive iteration bounds, leveraging a Helly-based conflict compression theory to avoid generic exponential cut explosion. In particular, for shallow networks with fixed input dimension, this establishes an unconditionally polynomial Benders iteration complexity in network size. Interval pruning, certificate transfer for pruned networks, and layerwise classical--Ising partitioning further reduce spin requirements. Experiments demonstrate exact certification fidelity for piecewise-linear networks and near-reference accuracy for non-linear activations under compact spin budgets. On MNIST benchmarks, Log-PW halves binary decision spins over One-Hot formulations, while Helly-based cuts achieve up to a $13.41\times$ speedup and an $87.6\%$ reduction in master queries over standard baselines.
item.dc:creator: Wenxin Li, Wenchao Liu, Anzhe Jiang, Weihao Li, Chuan Wang, Qi Gao, Yin Ma, Hai Wei, Kai Wen
